Title: Lyft's CEO says these 3 companies are getting business right
Full_Text: Lyft's CEO says these 3 companies are getting business right. David Risher touted three companies — Oura Ring, Starbucks, and Microsoft — for doing interesting things with their businesses.. David Risher.Courtesy of Lyft Lyft CEO David Risher said there were three companies he thought were successful in their businesses.He touted them for many reasons, from nailing cust… Lyft's CEO says these 3 companies are getting business right. Sherwood News wrote that when talking about a small company he admired, Risher pointed to the Oura Ring on his finger. He told the outlet that Oura Ring had "nailed the customer experience." Oura Ring is a health technology company founded in Finland. It makes smart rings ranging from $199 to $499 that track heart health, sleep patterns, activity, and stress levels, per the company's website. "It gives me enough information, and it doesn't feel naggy," he said to the outlet. "The technology is super slick and easy." Risher added, "They started with a clear idea, they've not tried to add 20 different things, and it's a really good example of a focused and customer-obsessed product." Speaking to Business Insider in June, Risher revealed that his Oura Ring was part of his morning routine. He said he checked the ring's report every morning after brushing his teeth to get insights into how well he had slept the night before.

Title: Lyft Expected to Post Higher 2Q Profit, Revenue -- Earnings Preview Published: Aug
Full_Text: Lyft Expected to Post Higher 2Q Profit, Revenue -- Earnings Preview Published: Aug. 5, 2025 at 11:53 a.m. ET Share Resize By Kelly Cloonan Lyft is set to post its second-quarter results Wednesday after the market closes. Here's what you need to know. REVENUE: The ride-hailing company is expected to report $1.61 billion in revenue, up from $1.44 billion in the same period a year ago, according to analysts polled by FactSet. Unpacking Axon Stock's Explosive Growth See All Videos PROFIT: Lyft is expected to post a quarterly profit of $16.2 million, or four cents a share, according to analysts polled by FactSet. This compares with $5 million, or one cent a share, for the same period a year earlier. Shares have risen about 8.5% in the past three months and recently traded around $14.33. WHAT TO WATCH: - Investors will be paying close attention to Lyft's plans to compete in an increasingly competitive autonomous ride market. Lyft said Monday it is teaming up with Baidu to deploy autonomous vehicles across Germany and the U.K. in 2026, adding the Chinese internet-search and technology company to its growing list of AV partnerships. But as AV companies scale and build out their own distribution capabilities, Lyft and Uber's dominance in the market could be at risk, Wedbush Securities analysts say. "While we think the near-term financial impact to established ridesharing platforms is limited, over time, we expect AVs will disrupt the current status quo," they say in a note. - Wall Street also will be keeping an eye on the San Francisco-based company's global expansion plans. Lyft recently scaled to Europe through its acquisition of taxi-hailing platform Freenow, and also has worked to boost its presence in Canada and smaller cities in the U.S. Those efforts, as well as its partnerships with companies like DoorDash, should give it a stronger competitive edge against Uber, Oppenheimer analysts say in a note.
